video_title: NBA’s punishment on Los Angeles Clippers was ‘eye opening’ | Not So Fast | NBA on NBC

quotes.speaker: Perloff
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA punishment for Clippers is significant and unprecedented
quotes.excerpt: Five first-round picks. That's not little. 30 million dollars, Steve Ballmer is not allowed to be in the facility.
quotes.quote: The NBA punishment when I saw it yesterday, five first-round picks. That's not little. 30 million dollars, Steve Ballmer is not allowed to be in the facility, participate, go to games, which he's always on the sidelines like Mark Cuban a generation ago. But this is the hammer. This isn't a mild hammer. This is the hammer.

quotes.speaker: Pabst
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers fans face a bleak future without draft assets
quotes.excerpt: You're losing five first-round picks. How can you get excited about the future of this team?
quotes.quote: If you're a Clippers fan, this is a raw deal. You're losing five first-round picks. How can you get excited about the future of this team? And they're expensive tickets. I understand hitting Ballmer, he deserves it, but the fans didn't do anything. And now, what do you do as a Clippers fan?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA punishment for Clippers is comparable to Timberwolves' 2000 penalty
quotes.excerpt: This is a comparable penalty to what the Minnesota Timberwolves received back in 2000.
quotes.quote: The severity of it was certainly eye-opening. This is a comparable penalty to what the Minnesota Timberwolves received back in 2000, and that was a clear case of cap circumvention. There was an email paper trail that had the Timberwolves dead to rights. This penalty tells me that the NBA believes that they've got the Clippers dead to rights.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA's decision to penalize Steve Ballmer is highly significant
quotes.excerpt: The fact that they went after Steve Ballmer spoke volumes here.
quotes.quote: The fact that they went after Steve Ballmer spoke volumes here. Nobody I talked to was really surprised that the NBA came down hard on the Clippers because they had a lot of evidence. You saw that 35-page report. There is a lot of smoldering guns out there that suggest the Clippers did a lot of impropriety when it came to the salary cap.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA sends a strong message to billionaire owners with suspension
quotes.excerpt: This is really the ultimate penalty that you can give a billionaire owner.
quotes.quote: This is really the ultimate penalty that you can give a billionaire owner, telling him that he can't be around the team, telling him he can't watch games in the arena that he built, that he can't be part of the board of governors meetings, that he can't be part of the NBA. This is something that I think Steve Ballmer is going to fight the hardest, and it surprised me a little that the NBA was willing to go there.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's influence in the NBA is unmatched
quotes.excerpt: He is the most influential owner, I would say, in the NBA.
quotes.quote: He is the most influential owner, I would say, in the NBA. Jerry Jones is like the de facto co-commissioner it feels like in the NFL. I wouldn't go that far with Steve Ballmer, but Steve Ballmer's ability through his net worth to make connections for the NBA globally, to be part of their development in technology, he sits on a lot of committees within the NBA. He is a loud voice, an influential voice at the board of governors meetings. He is as powerful a figure as they get in the NBA, and this is Adam Silver saying, we believe you did enough wrong to boot you out for a year.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA was never going to let the Clippers off lightly
quotes.excerpt: The NBA was never going to let the Clippers skate with just a slap on the wrist.
quotes.quote: Clearly the NBA was never going to let the Clippers skate with just a slap on the wrist. One of the most revealing things in the summary of the report is that we're not done. There's still a lot more. This is Wachtell Lipton saying, hey, we had to get this out. Adam Silver, the NBA, they were telling us to wrap this thing up, so here is what we got so far, but we want to be clear, there is more out there.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' punishment is the basketball equivalent of a death sentence
quotes.excerpt: It is the basketball equivalent of a death sentence.
quotes.quote: It is the basketball equivalent of a death sentence. It just is. There's some questions about whether or not, and I heard you bring this up at the top of the show, would the NBA restore some of these Clippers draft picks? They did to Minnesota. But the difference is that the Timberwolves ran their best behavior throughout that entire process. The Timberwolves didn't really fight it. They were dead to rights and they didn't fight it. They kind of took their punishment like men, and the NBA turned around in 2003 and said, you get a couple of these picks back.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers' combative response makes future leniency unlikely
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers are not going quietly into that night. Like, they are determined to fight.
quotes.quote: The Clippers are not going quietly into that night. Like, they are determined to fight. It sure sounds like they're considering legal options. That's not the behavior of an organization that's likely to get their picks back. So, they're not going to have a first-round pick till I believe 2035. And if you think about it contextually, guys, the player they're going to draft in the first round in 2035 is like 10 years old now.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA's punishment of Kawhi Leonard isolates the Clippers organization
quotes.excerpt: By giving Kawhi this slap on the wrist, they take Kawhi out of play.
quotes.quote: I'm sure the NBA wanted to come down harder on the Clippers or on Kawhi Leonard. But by giving Kawhi this slap on the wrist, they take Kawhi out of play. They take more importantly the union and its lawyers out of play. So now, they have isolated the Clippers here. They have removed arbitration from the table, they have removed the union from being a thorn in their side. This was the NBA saying, you know what, we don't like it, but it's more important to us to police the team and not the players.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer faces difficult decision regarding the Clippers' future
quotes.excerpt: Does he want to stick around and oversee a floundering franchise with a fan base?
quotes.quote: One of the big questions I have is, will Steve Ballmer sell this team? He's gone for a year. He paid two billion dollars for the team back in what, 2013? Even as a distressed asset, the Clippers can probably get 3x on that investment. He probably gets six billion. He owns the building, he sells that eight billion. Like, there's a lot of money to be made just by selling the Clippers. Steve Ballmer is 70 years old. Does he want to stick around and oversee a floundering franchise with a fan base that is going to blame him for the predicament that they're in?
